> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **250** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39e9a820fc57b5febd990a184194503b5687ad99` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `85317fe739013ac70771688d0abafebf6e9cb6e1` — the merge of head `27453659084258c8465f91f74b05b30022f471f4` into base `39e9a820fc57b5febd990a184194503b5687ad99`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 85317fe739013ac70771688d0abafebf6e9cb6e1 && git checkout 85317fe739013ac70771688d0abafebf6e9cb6e1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 39e9a820fc57b5febd990a184194503b5687ad99 27453659084258c8465f91f74b05b30022f471f4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 39e9a820fc57b5febd990a184194503b5687ad99 && git merge --no-ff 27453659084258c8465f91f74b05b30022f471f4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39e9a820fc57b5febd990a184194503b5687ad99
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 39e9a820fc57b5febd990a184194503b5687ad99` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jSpi3g1dQNTvN6zEuH

## 席位核对

L1 (L1-e) on head `75f97ca664`, card #33552: **REWORK**. One item is owed, in the declared change (the object label). The hidden-field half and the console half read correct.

**Owed: `link.object_label` is not "the object's label as `GET /meta/object/NAME` serves it" for a customized object.**
- The meta door translates with more than `metaTranslateOptions`. `meta-item-read-gate.ts:3662-3673` passes `packagedBase: packagedObjectBaseOf(p, 'object', name)` and the customization pair's bundles.
- `sharedObjectLabel` calls `translateObject({ name, label }, bundle, { locale, fallbackChain, defaultLocale })` with neither of those.
- In `translateObject`, `scalarOverridesPackagedBase(undefined, 'label', …)` judges nothing diverged, so the deployment catalog applies. `labelCatalogs` with no `pairBundle` never reads the pair's catalog (ADR-0146 D2).
- Two concrete cases:
  - A tenant who renamed the object (`objectExtensions` / a rename folded into `getSchema`), with a bundle entry for the packaged label: the meta door serves the rename, and the share page serves the bundle's translation of the old label.
  - A label translated only in the `<base>.custom` pair's catalog: the record page shows it, and the share page does not.
- The sentences that claim parity:
  - the module header: "is the object's label as `GET /meta/object/NAME` serves it";
  - the changeset: "translated the way `GET /meta/object/NAME` translates it".
- Fix it one of two ways, the dev's choice:
  - **(a)** Hand `sharedObjectLabel` the packaged base and the pair bundle on both mounts, so the answer is the meta door's. Pin a renamed object with a bundle entry: the rename stands.
  - **(b)** Narrow both sentences to what is served (the bundle over the folded declared label, without the packaged-base or pair rules), file a card for the divergence, and name it in the body.

**Read and accepted**
- **Shape** (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36460`, CLEAN): open, draft, base `main`, `Fixes #33552`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, which is right (two optional answer keys and an optional fourth argument), `Metadata-protocol: none`. One changeset covers all four published packages. Gates at this head: 62 success, 14 expected skip, 0 failed.
- **Hidden fields.** `projectField` sets `hidden: true` only for `field.hidden === true`. The page drops a field marked hidden on top of the existing system, audit and declared-only rules. That is the record panel's rule. `hidden` is display only and does not redact (the value still rides `record`), which matches the card's ask and the record page. Redaction stays `redactFields`.
- **Both mounts** call the one builder with `{ acceptLanguage, i18n }`. The plugin resolves `i18n` per request, guarded. The runtime twin uses `deps.resolveService(context, 'i18n')`, guarded, with null mapped to undefined. A throwing service falls back to the declared label, and the resolve never fails on it.
- **Locale.** `preferredLocaleFromHeader(Accept-Language)` comes first, then the service default: the meta door's order. The console sends `<html lang>` as `Accept-Language` on resolve and messages, and omits the header when empty.
- **Console.** The title reads `object_label || object_name`, so an older server or an unlabelled object keeps the name.
- **Caching nit, no action.** The answer now varies by `Accept-Language`, but `Vary` is still `SHARE_PASSWORD_VARY`. Harmless: both mounts send `Cache-Control: no-store`, and a label is not a secret.
- **Changeset, checked sentence by sentence.** It is true apart from the parity sentence above. That includes "An object that declares no label carries no `object_label`" (`textOf(schema.label)`) and the `hidden` absent-when-false rule.

A delta ACCEPT follows on a head that makes one of (a) or (b) true, with its pin or card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `75f97ca6645c67d7aff5dd4b2da6774a0ca0d837`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #33552 body and its four comments (triage 6886911138, regrade 6984990301, claim 7077759641, dev report 7079233796); PR #36460 body and its two comments; the net diff of 12 files against merge base 4e55e4eb; the check-runs on this head. Every check-run on this head is success or skipped. None failed and none is pending.

### ① Derived judgments

- `link.object_label` on the resolve answer. Right. It is optional in the type (`ShareLinkResolvedLink` gains `object_label?: string`). It is spread in only when the schema declares a label, so an unlabelled object answers the same nine link keys as before. The types test pins that. A reader that ignores the key is unaffected. The name follows the seat ruling quoted in the PR body.
- `fields[NAME].hidden` on the resolve answer. Right. It is optional and typed `hidden?: true`. `projectField` sets it only when `field.hidden === true`, and `FieldSchema.hidden` is a boolean in spec. A shown field carries no key, so an existing reader sees no change for it.
- Same shape on both mounts. Right. Both the plugin-sharing route and the runtime dispatcher twin call the one builder, `buildShareLinkResolveAnswer`, with the same four inputs: the record, the resolution, `getSchema(object_name)` on the request's ObjectQL, and the request's `Accept-Language` with the i18n service. The runtime harness runs both mounts over real ObjectQL and SQLite, and asserts equal data under a zh-CN request.
- Same hidden rule on both mounts. Right. The flag is computed in one place, `projectField` in `@objectstack/types`, from the schema each mount passes. Neither mount computes it itself. The harness checks an authored hidden field and the injected `queue` column on each mount.
- Locale rule. Right, and it matches the body. The locale is `preferredLocaleFromHeader(Accept-Language)`, else `getDefaultLocale()`, as the meta door reads it. The resolve options match `metaTranslateOptions` in `@objectstack/rest`: the declared fallback as the chain, and `sourceLocale` before `defaultLocale` as the authored language. The bundle is built the way `translationBundleOf` builds it. A missing service, no locale, an empty bundle or a throw returns the declared label. The body says the packaged-base and pair-bundle overlay inputs are not used, and they are not.
- i18n resolution per mount. Right. The plugin resolves `ctx.getService('i18n')` per request inside a try. The twin calls `deps.resolveService(context, 'i18n')` with no environment id, which is how `domains/meta.ts` resolves it for the meta door.
- New optional inputs. Right and additive. `buildShareLinkResolveAnswer` gains an optional fourth argument. `ShareLinkRoutesOptions` gains an optional `i18n` resolver. A caller that passes neither gets the declared label and the hidden flags.
- New exports from `@objectstack/types` (through its `export *`): `sharedObjectLabel`, `ShareLinkLabelI18n` and `ShareLinkAnswerLocale`. Additive and right. The changeset does not name them. No existing reader is misled by an unlisted addition, so this is not graded.
- Console share page. Right. The header prints `object_label`, else `object_name`. `SharedRecordFields` drops a key whose projection says `hidden: true`, which is the rule `RecordDetailPanel` uses. With no projection, nothing new is dropped. `shareRequestHeaders` sends the html element's lang attribute as `Accept-Language` on the resolve and messages requests, the same source the settings calls read. The header is CORS-safelisted, so no preflight is added. The local `ShareLink` and `SharedFieldDisplay` types gain the two optional keys.
- Body claims against the code. They match. Each change the body names is in the diff, and the diff has no change of contract the body leaves out. `packages/spec/src` is untouched, as claimed.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/33552-share-link-label-hidden.md` names `@objectstack/types`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@object-ui/console`, each at `patch`. These are exactly the four packages the diff changes in published source.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. The answer gains two optional members and the functions gain optional inputs. Nothing is removed, renamed or tightened.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No key, value or type a metadata author can write changes. `hidden` and `label` are read, not added.
- The level follows from the kind. `none` takes `patch` under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Both declaration lines are in the PR body and in the changeset body. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions, the key name (`link.object_label` or a top-level `objectLabel`). Answered: option A, by seat ruling as the PR body records. It is right on the merits. It sits beside `object_name`, which the page already reads.
- Deviation, the runtime dispatcher twin was outside the claimed file surface. Answered: in scope by seat ruling. It is right on the merits. The route has two producers, and leaving the twin out would make the two mounts answer different shapes.
- Deviation, one test run was not under the lock, and the derived gates ran while a source file was mutated. Answered: the check-runs on this head cover them. Every one is green.
- Deviation, the changeset level was copied from the claim. Answered: `patch` is right, see ②.
- out_of_scope_findings[0], the field labels in the projection stay authored. Answered: outside this card's acceptance, which asks for the object label only. A follow-up card is the seat's call.
- out_of_scope_findings[1], the shared `Vary` does not list `Accept-Language`. Escalated as S1 below.
- Triage stop rule (FLS). The dev reports that `owning_business_unit_id` and `queue` carry no `requiredPermissions` or `maskingRule` at their source, so the rule did not trigger. Nothing in the diff contradicts that.
- SQL push-down. No finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The label is read from the schema and the i18n bundle, and the hidden flag from the schema.

S1 (should-fix) — The resolve answer now varies on `Accept-Language`, but both mounts still send `Vary: SHARE_PASSWORD_VARY`, which lists only the two password headers. Both mount docblocks say that `Vary` exists for a cache that does not honour `no-store`. Such a cache could now serve one reader's localized label to a reader in another language. The dev noted this and filed nothing. Add `Accept-Language` to the `Vary` the two public routes send, or file it as its own card before this one closes.

No must-fix.

Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC`

## 席位核对

L1 (L1-e) delta on head `27453659084258c8465f91f74b05b30022f471f4`, card #33552: **ACCEPT**. This supersedes REWORK 7079684282 (head `75f97ca664`). The short delta L2 owns the `Vary` reading (its S1).

**The owed item: closed, by option (a).**
- `sharedObjectLabel` now hands `translateObject` the object's packaged base.
  - It is read the way the meta door's `packagedObjectBaseOf(p, 'object', name)` reads it: the protocol's `getPackagedObjectBase(name)`, called synchronously, with `undefined` on no protocol, no accessor, or a throw.
  - Both mounts resolve the `'protocol'` service per request, guarded: the plugin through `ctx.getService`, the runtime twin through `deps.resolveService(context, 'protocol')`.
  - A served label that diverged from the packaged one (a rename) therefore reads no deployment catalog, which is ADR-0029 D9.2a, as on the meta door.
- **No pair bundle: I checked the reason, and it holds.**
  - At `meta-item-read-gate.ts` ~3660 the meta door also passes `pairBundle` and `patchBundles`. For an object, `pairTranslationBundleOf` has no served override base (objects are extended, ADR-0146 D10).
  - `patchBundles` (#33952) reach only field slots: `translateObject`'s `patchCatalogsOf`, "a field slot of an object that a code package's `fieldPatches` changed". The object label is not one.
  - `getPackagedObjectBase` keeps the owner's `label`, so an extension's rename counts as diverged on both doors alike.
  - For the label, the share answer and the meta door now take the same inputs.
- **New pins**, on the builder and on both mounts:
  - a renamed object with a bundle entry for its packaged label keeps the rename;
  - control: an object still on its packaged label is translated;
  - a protocol that cannot answer is read as no baseline known.
- **Sentences.** The module header and the changeset now spell out the inputs (the served label, `metaTranslateOptions`, the packaged base, no `pairBundle` and why). "A renamed object therefore keeps its rename" is true of the code.

**Also in the delta (the L2's S1).**
- `SHARE_LINK_PUBLIC_VARY` = the password pair plus `Accept-Language`, from one constant in `@objectstack/types`.
- It is answered on `/resolve` and `/messages` on both mounts, with `Cache-Control: no-store` unchanged. The header tests follow it.
- The changeset states the new `Vary` value and the new optional `protocol` resolver.

**`27453659`** is test-harness only: the two share-link header harnesses pay the metadata load at collection.

**Gates at this head:** 60 success, 12 expected skip, 0 failed, mergeable `clean`. Everything else in 7079684282 stands as read.

repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `27453659084258c8465f91f74b05b30022f471f4`
Local-runs: none

Delta review: `75f97ca6..27453659`. Prior record 7079728874 (PASS at `75f97ca6`) stands for everything this delta leaves alone.

Read: card #33552 and every comment on it, the dev delta 7079994565 included; PR #36460 body and its comments, with the L1-e REWORK 7079684282 and the final-green note 7080388304; the compare `75f97ca6...27453659`; the check-runs on this head. The compare is two commits, `ec70ad9c` and `27453659`, each with one parent on the branch. There is no merge of main in the delta, so every hunk below is the dev's. Ten files change. Every check-run on this head is success or skipped (Test Core 10 of 10 and Test UI 16 of 16 among them). None failed and none is pending. The PR is mergeable clean.

### ① Derived judgments

- `sharedObjectLabel` passes `packagedBase`. Right, and it matches the meta door. `translateMetaDocument` and `translateMetaList` in `@objectstack/rest` hand the object translator `packagedObjectBaseOf(p, 'object', name)`. That is the protocol's `getPackagedObjectBase(name)` (the `object` row of `PACKAGED_BASE_ACCESSORS`), read synchronously, with `undefined` for no protocol, no accessor or a throw. The new reader does the same, and `sharedObjectLabel` already refuses an empty name before it is called. In `translateObject` the label goes through `resolveScalar('label')`. When the served label differs from the packaged one and no pair bundle is given, the deployment catalog is not read, so a rename stands. That is the meta door's answer.
- "Objects are extend-only, so no pair bundle." True. `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION.object` in `packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts` is `extend_only` (ADR-0146 D10). `servedOverrideBaseOf` in `metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts` answers `undefined` for any type that `isOverridableMetadataType` refuses. So `pairTranslationBundleOf(p, 'object', document)` on the meta door is always `undefined`, and that door hands the object translator no pair catalog either. The second L1 case, a label translated only in a `.custom` pair's catalog, cannot arise for an object.
- The meta door's other object inputs do not reach the label. `patchBundles` (#33952) is read only for field slots (`patchCatalogsOf` in `translateObject`). `withoutStaleObjectPlural` rewrites only `pluralLabel`. Neither is a gap for `link.object_label`.
- Protocol resolution per mount. Right. The runtime twin calls `deps.resolveService(context, 'protocol')` inside a try, which is how `domains/meta.ts` `resolveProtocol` reads it.
